official.deadline_note: No separate scholarship deadline exists: the award is requested inside the admission application, so the admission window governs. Fall 2027 round 1 runs 15 October 2026 (13:00) to 4 December 2026 (23:59) and round 2 runs 1 March 2027 (13:00) to 15 May 2027 (23:59).
official.application_cycle: Spring 2027 intake (current round) and Fall 2027 intakes
official.status_note: The university's Key Dates page lists the Spring 2027 online application window as open until 14 October 2026 (23:59), with the Fall 2027 first round opening on 15 October 2026. The scholarship page instructs applicants to request the scholarship when applying for admission on the online system and warns that the scholarship is subject to change, with the admission brochure for that semester as accurate.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'Tuition and miscellaneous fees are waived or reduced as part of the scholarship' (doctoral degree programmes).
benefits: Tuition and miscellaneous fees are waived or reduced as part of the scholarship for new international students in doctoral degree programmes
Stipend of NT$50,000 per semester for doctoral degree programmes
Stipend is disbursed in monthly instalments of NT$10,000 after the recipient completes registration for the semester
The scholarship is awarded for eight consecutive semesters, beginning in the semester for which the recipient was granted admission and after registration
eligibility: Must be a new international student applying for admission to a Fu Jen Catholic University doctoral degree programme under the university's foreign student admission brochure
Must not have received scholarships or subsidies set by Taiwan government agencies for pursuing a degree (Regulation Article 2)
Master's degree holders are eligible for doctoral programmes (education qualification)
Nationality and residence rules follow the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan
As a rule, one recipient per doctoral programme holding a foreign-student admission quota per academic year (Regulation Article 3)
Funding follows the admission decision, and registration for the semester of admission must be completed for the award to begin
requirements: Request the scholarship when applying for admission on the online system
Apply online and submit required documents within the published application period; hard-copy applications are not accepted
Pay the application fee (NT$1,600 applying from within Taiwan, US$65 from overseas, per programme; non-refundable) and upload the receipt within the application period
Complete registration for the semester of admission for the scholarship to begin
Satisfy the admission requirements of the doctoral programme applied for, including department-specified documents
documents: Certificate or diploma of the highest degree (notarised Chinese or English translation if the original is in another language)
Complete academic transcripts issued by the school for each year of study (notarised translation if in another language)

Financial proof issued within the last 3 months by a banking institution showing funds equivalent to TWD$200,000 or more, or official proof of a full scholarship; must not be issued by agents, companies or individuals
Receipt for the application fee, using the dedicated remittance details downloaded from the system after Step 1
Verification of nationality, e.g. a photocopy of a passport valid for 1 year or more
Declaration Form downloaded from the application system, plus additional documents required by the department or graduate programme
selection_criteria: Applications are received by the International Student Center of the Office of International and Cross-Strait Education, reviewed by each doctoral programme, then re-reviewed by the university's International Academic Exchange Review Committee (Regulation Article 8)
Approved recipients are announced on the university's foreign student admission website

Applicants may upload supporting documents such as Chinese or English language test certificates, international competition award certificates and proofs of published articles or papers, with Chinese or English translations (Regulation Article 5)

Continuation requires enrolling in at least 2 credits per semester; the award is cancelled for failure to register or withdrawal, major misconduct records, two semesters with grades below 80 points, no supervising professor willing to guide for more than 3 months, concurrent study at another domestic school, or unauthorised absence from Taiwan exceeding 1 month (Regulation Article 7)
coverage: Tuition and miscellaneous fees waived or reduced across the eight-semester doctoral award
Living-expense stipend of NT$50,000 per semester, paid as monthly instalments of NT$10,000 after registration
Support begins in the semester of admission once registration is completed
application_method: Confirm eligibility as an international student under the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan
Confirm the doctoral programme intended is open to international students for that academic year in the admission brochure
Read the graduation regulations of the programme via the programme website or office
Apply online and submit required documents at http://idsasys.oie.fju.edu.tw/ within the application period (paper submissions are not accepted)
Request the scholarship inside the admission application, pay the application fee through the system's dedicated remittance details and upload the receipt
If admitted, submit the Intent to Enroll by the published deadline and complete registration for the semester
official.application_route: Online only through the FJCU Application System for International Students (http://idsasys.oie.fju.edu.tw/); the scholarship is requested inside the admission application with no separate form.
official.citizenship_residency: Foreign nationality under the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan: applicants who have never held R.O.C. nationality, or who have resided overseas continuously for at least six years (eight years for medicine, dentistry or Chinese medicine) with no more than 120 days in Taiwan per calendar year; Hong Kong or Macau permanent residents need continuous residence outside Taiwan for at least six years. Applying to study in Taiwan under this route is limited to one application, except when progressing to a master's or higher programme after completing a degree.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the award is specifically for new foreign (international) students admitted to FJCU doctoral degree programmes.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to doctoral programmes that carry a foreign-student admission quota, with as a rule one recipient per programme per academic year; applicants who already hold Taiwan government degree scholarships or subsidies are excluded.
official.research_requirement: Doctoral applicants must hold a master's degree and meet the applied programme's admission requirements. No separate research proposal is published for the scholarship itself, but applicants may upload proofs of published articles or papers as supporting documents.
official.duration: Eight consecutive semesters for doctoral degree programmes, beginning in the semester for which the recipient was granted admission and after registration is completed.
official.description: Fu Jen Catholic University states the scholarship was established to support the government's policy of expanding the recruitment of foreign students and to strengthen the recruitment of outstanding foreign students to doctoral study at the university. For new international students in doctoral degree programmes, the university publishes an award covering eight consecutive semesters in which tuition and miscellaneous fees are waived or reduced and the recipient receives a stipend of NT$50,000 per semester, disbursed in monthly instalments of NT$10,000 after registration.
official.program_type: Institutional (Fu Jen-funded) scholarship for new international doctoral students
official.english_requirement: No English score is published for the scholarship itself. The university's official Language Qualification Requirements document sets thresholds per department using TOCFL listening and reading (Levels 2-6 by band) or HSK (Levels 4-6), plus a CEFR-based English comparison chart: B1 - TOEFL iBT 42 / TOEFL ITP 433 / IELTS 4-5 / TOEIC 550; B2 - 72 / 543 / IELTS 5.5-6.5 / 785; C1 - 95 / 620 / IELTS 7-8 / 945; C2 - 114 / IELTS 9. Three doctoral programmes are listed as English-taught (Applied Science and Engineering, Chemistry, and Comparative Literature and Cross-Cultural Studies).

applicant_utility.summary: This is an admission-embedded award rather than a standalone competition: you request it by ticking the scholarship option inside the FJCU online admission application for a doctoral programme, and funding follows the admission decision. Doctoral recipients receive tuition and miscellaneous fees waived or reduced plus NT$50,000 per semester, paid as NT$10,000 monthly instalments after registration, in principle for eight consecutive semesters. Because the rule allows only one recipient per doctoral programme per academic year as a principle, and excludes anyone already funded by a Taiwan government degree scholarship, admission strength and your programme choice decide the outcome more than any separate scholarship essay.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International master's graduates with a strong academic record applying to an FJCU doctoral programme, especially the English-taught doctoral programmes, who can self-fund living costs at the start of the semester.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your chosen doctoral programme lists foreign-student quota places in the current semester's admission brochure before starting the application

Prepare a bank-issued financial statement dated within the last three months showing at least TWD$200,000 (or official full-scholarship proof) - documents from agents, companies or individuals are refused
Book any required TOCFL, HSK or English test early and have non-Chinese/English certificates and transcripts notarised in advance
Keep your passport valid for more than one year, pay the application fee via the system's applicant-specific remittance details, and upload the receipt before the window closes
Line up a potential supervisor early, because no professor willing to guide you for more than three months cancels the award
common_rejection_risks: Breaking the foreign-student residence rules, such as spending more than 120 days in Taiwan in a calendar year or having studied in Taiwan as an overseas Chinese student
Financial proof that is older than three months or issued by an agent, company or individual instead of a banking institution
Applying to a doctoral programme that carries no foreign-student admission quota that academic year, since the quota is one award per programme as a rule
Failing to upload the application-fee receipt inside the application window, or paying it late or combined with another applicant's payment
Holding a Taiwan government degree scholarship or subsidy, which makes you ineligible for this award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Dormitory costs about NT$9,000-31,000 per person per semester plus a NT$3,000 deposit, and the university lists insurance, accommodation and books as separate study-related costs; the non-refundable application fee (NT$1,600 from within Taiwan or US$65 from overseas) is paid before admission.
document_audit: The financial statement must be issued by a banking institution within the last 3 months and show at least TWD$200,000 - the university explicitly rejects documents from agents, companies or individuals
Any degree certificate or transcript not in Chinese or English needs a notarised Chinese or English translation
Remittance details are applicant-specific: download them from the system after completing Step 1 and never combine your payment with other applicants
The Declaration Form must be downloaded from the application system itself, and the passport used for nationality verification must be valid for at least one more year
alerts: The Spring 2027 application window closes on 14 October 2026 at 23:59, within days of this record being verified; the Fall 2027 first round opens immediately on 15 October 2026 and a second round runs 1 March to 15 May 2027
The university warns that scholarship terms are subject to change and that the admission brochure for the relevant semester is authoritative - re-check it each cycle

The award lapses if you fail to register, take fewer than 2 credits in a semester, record two semesters below 80 points, go more than three months without a supervising professor, study concurrently at another Taiwanese school, or stay outside Taiwan for over a month without approval
The stipend only starts after you complete registration for the semester, so budget for the first weeks of the semester before the first NT$10,000 instalment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Everything is submitted in one pass inside the FJCU online application system during the published window - application form, documents, fee receipt and the scholarship request together - after which the doctoral programme reviews the file and the International Academic Exchange Review Committee re-reviews it, with outcomes announced on the foreign student admission site.
